Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Raspberries, blackberries, and wineberries

The catalogue recalls bramble fruits in jams, pies, flavorings, and dried foods. It distinguishes introduced wineberries and records elders’ concern that wild blackberries had become harder to find by 2014. The plants fed wildlife as well as people.1

The catalogue names Church Street, Little Beach Road, and Dump Road in memories of wild blackberries becoming harder to find.1

Places named in the catalogue

Shinnecock territories; Church Street; Little Beach Road; Dump Road.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF p. 19. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
